title: cwf-continental-united-states
label: Dr. Doom

won.source: No document records when Dr. Doom won the CWF United States Championship. The fed's own Title Histories page lists no former holder; the fed's own Current Champions page names him the reigning champion. Read together, this is the belt's own founding/only reign in the held record; the won date is approximated to the fed's own founding (circa 2000), which is the earliest the reign could have begun.

how: The belt's own founding/only reign in the held record — no document records how or when he won it.

title: cwf-continental-hardcore
label: Mike Maddness

won.source: No document records exactly when Mike Maddness won the CWF Hardcore Championship, but the corpus bounds it tightly: the fed's own served Friday Night Blitz broadcast (18 January 2002) has him winning only the #1 CONTENDERSHIP for the belt, beating Xtreme T through a trash can -- meaning he was not yet champion that night. The fed's own served "Babylon" results (25 January 2002) already bill him as champion, defending successfully against eXodus. The title changed hands, off-page and unrecorded, sometime in the seven days between the two shows; the Title Histories page's own "n/a" former-champion listing is consistent with the vacant belt simply being awarded to the newly-earned #1 contender rather than won in a documented match.

how: Earned the #1 contendership by beating Xtreme T through a trash can at Friday Night Blitz (18 January 2002); became champion off-page sometime in the following week, no document recording how. Successfully defended against eXodus at 'Babylon' (25 January 2002).
note: No linked event: the reign's own won date is unknown, and the linked Babylon show only captures a defense, not the winning of the title, so the ambiguity is left recorded rather than resolved.
